name: Default prices, quantity tiers, customer-group prices and account contract prices

dependsOn.why: The list price is patched onto a product the catalogue created; this recipe finds products by number and creates none.
The customer group, the account's customer number and the buyer the probes sign in as are that recipe's objects.

mcpOnly.reason: Every step has an MCP find, write and read-back (get_products_by_sku, patch_products_safe, get_user_groups, save_user_groups, get_prices_by_product_id, save_prices). The behavioural probes read the delivery API: no MCP tool returns the price a visitor or a signed-in user is charged, so an MCP-only run reports them OPEN.

hosted.reason: Every step is MCP; the probes are delivery API reads; no SQL.

steps.title: Give each priced product its default price (the product's own price)

bindings.reason: A product is created, grouped and indexed by the catalogue recipe; this recipe prices products that exist and never creates one.

steps.trap: The default price is the product's own field (patch_products_safe defaultPrice), not a price-matrix row; patch_products_safe writes only the members it is given.

steps.title: Ensure the user group the group prices are scoped to
steps.trap: A group price reaches the group's direct members only; the users.accounts recipe makes the buyer a direct member.

steps.title: Write each quantity tier as an unscoped price row at its quantity
steps.trap: A price row's scope is the set of members it carries; the read leaves out every null member, so a tier is found by stating each scope member null, or a contract row at the same quantity would match it.

steps.title: Write each customer-group price as a row scoped to the user group
steps.trap: userGroupId is a user group (PriceUserGroupId); customerGroupId matches a customer number despite its name, and a user-group id there saves and matches nobody.

steps.title: Write each account contract price as a row scoped to the account's customer number
steps.trap: Lowest matching price wins, not the most specific scope: a tier below the contract amount undercuts the contract for the account too.

probes.title: An anonymous visitor is served each product's default price

bindings.reason: No MCP tool returns the price a visitor or a signed-in user is charged: get_prices_by_product_id lists the stored rows, which the steps already read back, and force_price_recalculation prices an order without the frontend user's context.

probes.title: An anonymous visitor is offered each quantity tier at its break

bindings.reason: No MCP tool returns the price a visitor or a signed-in user is charged: get_prices_by_product_id lists the stored rows, which the steps already read back, and force_price_recalculation prices an order without the frontend user's context.

probes.title: The signed-in buyer pays its account's contract price

bindings.reason: No MCP tool returns the price a visitor or a signed-in user is charged: get_prices_by_product_id lists the stored rows, which the steps already read back, and force_price_recalculation prices an order without the frontend user's context.

probes.title: The signed-in buyer, a member of the customer group, pays each group price

bindings.reason: No MCP tool returns the price a visitor or a signed-in user is charged: get_prices_by_product_id lists the stored rows, which the steps already read back, and force_price_recalculation prices an order without the frontend user's context.

probes.title: The signed-in buyer is offered each quantity tier at its break

bindings.reason: No MCP tool returns the price a visitor or a signed-in user is charged: get_prices_by_product_id lists the stored rows, which the steps already read back, and force_price_recalculation prices an order without the frontend user's context.

provenOn.evidence: commerce.customer-prices.1-verify.json (one default price WOULD-UPDATE, every price row WOULD-CREATE, probes FAIL), the first apply (default price updated, tier and group rows created, every probe that needed only those PASS in the same run, no debt), commerce.customer-prices.2-apply.json (contract created, 11 of 11), 3-verify and 4-apply-again (11 of 11, nothing written), 6-apply-update and 7-apply-restore (tier and contract updated in place and served at once, 11 of 11), 8-final-verify and 9-hosted-verify without SQL (11 of 11); 5-mcponly.json is 6 of 11, every step PASS and the five delivery probes OPEN. The anonymous visitor was served the default price and the tier, the signed-in buyer the contract, group and tier prices; a delivery API cart charged 8 at quantity 10 against a default of 10 for an anonymous visitor, and 7 to the buyer whose contract is 7.

the whole-build recipe set on a fresh fictional input after the add-in was rolled 0.6.3-BETA -> 0.6.6-BETA (Update-HostAddIn): 1-verify (all eleven recipes WOULD-CREATE), 2-apply, 3-verify (11 of 11 recipes), 4-apply-again (nothing written, no debt owed), 5-verify after a brand restore (11 of 11); the same input then verified 11 of 11 on the add-in rolled back to 0.6.3. 6-mcponly is an MCP-only apply on a second fresh input. This recipe: 11 of 11, the buyer served the contract, group and tier prices; MCP-only 6 of 11, every step PASS and the delivery probes not observable.

the same delivered-copy site: the copy's quantity-1 group and contract rows found at quantity 1 (UNCHANGED), 12 steps UNCHANGED, no WOULD-CREATE, -Apply wrote nothing (price rows 19 before and after). From empty [mcp 0.6.6-BETA]: the group and contract rows written at quantity 1, 11 of 11 with the signed-in buyer served the contract, group and tier prices.

traps: A price write needs no debt: the delivery API product read and the cart served a changed default price, a new or updated tier, group or contract row on the next request, with no cache flush, index build or recycle.
On 10.30.6 the stock cart honours an unscoped quantity tier (the 10.28 line ignored it), and the lowest matching price wins: a tier below a contract amount undercuts the contract for the account too.
The MCP price read leaves out every null member: a scope is matched by stating each scope member null, never by its absence alone.
customerGroupId on save_prices matches a customer number; a user group goes in userGroupId and reaches direct members only.

A group or contract price without a quantity is written at quantity 1, the natural key a layer copy writes too (a price row applies from its quantity, so 1 and 0 serve the same buyer), so a copy's rows are found and not written a second time. A row an earlier build wrote at quantity 0 is not found at 1: remove it, or state quantity 0 in the input.
